evidence: Authored for this product: instruction.md:1-17 is a first-person recruiting-team ask specific to HireOps (pipeline board per job, interview places, colleague-named refusals, all-or-none multi-move with undo, 15 s live updates that preserve note/cursor/open card, recruiter-candidate conversations with paged history, per-person unread, seen marks, per-person drafts surviving sign-out, candidate wording). hireops_rules.md sections 1-9 carry product-specific rules (six stages incl. Rejected off to the side; rejected-from stage + reopen only there; manual in-stage order shared by all; undo invalidated by later moves but not by notes; candidate wording table; seen semantics excluding the Observer). task.toml:22-32 identity is coherent and product-specific (name turing/hireops-recruiting-operations, arena_slice recruiting-hiring-operations, provenance 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task'), consistent with NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT 'Describe the assigned product domain accurately'. Criteria are authored, not copied: functional/judge.toml has 38 hro_* binary criteria tied to HireOps protocols Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D in functional/prompt.md:59-85 naming the seeded people (Rafael Costa, Mei Lin, Ingrid Sorensen, Noor Haddad's 120-message Platform Engineer thread, Lena Fischer's seeded unread count 1). Visual criteria were re-authored from the template (template 'visual_typography' generic text vs task hro_vis_type 'Judge desktop typography on the board, conversations and activity'). Residue grep over the task (excluding seed) for pellmoor|threadline|vacanc|channel|bazaar|torquebay|docketlight|gridforge|patchpad|colderwater|boardloom|change_me|merchant|ballot found only the browser API 'BroadcastChannel' in solution/app/public/js/app.js:139. Sibling comparison: the nearest sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (same recruiting domain, also one-stage moves, capacity, atomic batch, stale 409). It is not a nouns-swap: Pellmoor's 60 criteria centre on panels and 1-5 scoring, assessment-version invalidation, d3 funnel loss attribution, offer-opening capacity (reserved/filled), durable actor-scoped retry receipts and batch review/preview (hiring-rules.md), none of which appear in HireOps; HireOps' core (shared manual card order, single-level undo with conflict rules, non-disruptive live board, staff-candidate messaging with unread/seen/paging/drafts, candidate portal isolation with stage wording) is absent from Pellmoor. Different arena_slice (full-stack-typescript-d3-esbuild-express-sqlite-pipeline vs recruiting-hiring-operations) and stack. projects/threadline-chat shares only generic chat ideas (unread counts, load older without jumping: instruction.md:61,97-108) inside a Slack-style channels/threads/reactions product; HireOps' conversation layer is per-application, two-sided staff/candidate with seen marks and session-surviving drafts. Overlapping concurrency mechanics (stale-version 409, all-or-none batch) are suite-wide reusable patterns the authoring context explicitly encourages reusing ('Reuse validated infrastructure and components, but author distinct domain behavior'). Counterexample probes: a reviewer attempting to map HireOps criteria onto Pellmoor by renaming vacancy->job, offer capacity->interview places finds no counterpart for 20+ HireOps criteria (hro_reorder, hro_live_board, hro_thread_*, hro_unread_*, hro_seen, hro_drafts, hro_candidate_*), so no nouns-swap reading holds; conversely no Pellmoor-only artefact (funnel, panel scores, receipts) leaks into HireOps. Caveats recorded, not defects: (1) no written suite domain plan exists in the workspace (grep for 'domain plan'/'arena_slice' in authoring docs found none), so 'fits the suite's domain plan' was judged from the assignment provenance and sibling slices; (2) two tasks now occupy the recruiting domain (Pellmoor, HireOps), which is a portfolio-planning observation for the lead rather than a clone defect. This row is source-only; it needs no runtime evidence and I did not rely on raw-evidence-index.json. No Oracle, model or portal score is implied.
